newsitem.title: USA: Cisco buys high-speed network business.
newsitem.headline: Cisco buys high-speed network business.

text.p: Cisco Systems Inc on Monday said it agreed to buy the high-speed networking business of Integrated Network Corp. for roughly $125 million in cash and stock in a deal that the networking equipment giant expects will temporarily cut its earnings.

Cisco said it would pay $108 million in cash to buy Integrated Network's Dagaz xDSL unit, and also 230,000 shares of Cisco stock, valued at about $16.5 million, to cover the costs of funding of Integrated's employee stock option plan.
In exchange, Cisco will acquire Dagaz xDSL's products and intellectual property, personnel and other high-speed network-related assets.
In connection with the deal, Cisco said it planned to take a charge of between 8 and 11 cents per share against after-tax earnings during its first fiscal 1998 quarter ending in October.
Cisco said it expected the transaction to have a neutral impact on its earnings for the fiscal 1998 year as a whole and to have a positive effect on its results thereafter.

The Dagaz system uses an emerging technology called Digital Subscriber Line to allow phone carriers to offer high-speed data, video and voice service to customers over existing copper telephone lines.

The telephone line technology has begun to be embraced by major phone service providers as a low-cost method for delivering high-speed, two-way interactive Internet services to residential and business customers.
Cisco has set itself a goal of creating high-speed data networks with the size, scale and reliability of the public phone network.

It said Integrated Network Corp's technology is ready to handle large numbers of phone customers, integrate with existing phone networks and is capable of splitting voice and data traffic, relieving congestion on existing phone networks.
The Dagaz purchase has been approved by the boards of both companies and is expected to be completed in August, Cisco said.

Cisco said it eventually plans to relocate the operations of Bridgewater, N.J.-based Intergrated Network Corp. to its Chelmsford, Mass. facility, where it operates various research facilities. Cisco is based in San Jose, Calif.
Cisco stock fell $1.06 to $78.625 in Monday morning trading on volume of nearly two million shares.
